cleanliness: The property of being cleanly, or habitually clean; good hygiene.
complicity: The state of being complicit; involvement as a partner or accomplice, especially in a crime or other wrongdoing.
fray: To (cause to) unravel; used particularly for the edge of something made of cloth, or the end of a rope.
frock: A dress, a piece of clothing for a female, which consists of a skirt and a cover for the upper body.
duds: A device or machine that is useless because it does not work properly or has failed to work, such as a bomb, or explosive projectile.
mislead: To lead astray, in a false direction.
impetuous: Making arbitrary decisions, especially in an impulsive and forceful manner.
oar: A type of lever used to propel a boat, having a flat blade at one end and a handle at the other, and pivoted in a rowlock atop the gunwale, whereby a rower seated in the boat and pulling the handle can pass the blade through the water by repeated strokes against the water's resistance, thus moving the boat .
enmity: The quality of being an enemy; hostile or unfriendly disposition.
parchment: Material, made from the polished skin of a calf, sheep, goat or other animal, used like paper for writing.
trays: A small, typically rectangular or round, flat, and rigid object upon which things are carried.
annihilated: To reduce to nothing, to destroy, to eradicate.
appetizer: A small, light, and usually savory first course in a meal
congratulated: To express one’s sympathetic pleasure or joy to the person(s) it is felt for.
xu: A minor unit of currency in Vietnam, now little-used, forming a hundredth of a dong.
defenders: Someone who defends people or property
bland: Having a soothing effect; not irritating or stimulating.
anointed: To smear or rub over with oil or an unctuous substance; also, to spread over, as oil.
exorcist: A person, especially a priest, who practices exorcism.
dehydrated: To lose or remove water; to dry
fractures: An instance of breaking, a place where something has broken.
enforced: To keep up, impose or bring into effect something, not necessarily by force.
billiard: A shot in billiards or snooker in which the cue ball strikes two other balls; a carom.
flamingo: A wading bird of the family Phoenicopteridae.
hydra: Any of several small freshwater polyps of the genus Hydra and related genera, having a naked cylindrical body and an oral opening surrounded by tentacles.
idols: A graven image or representation of anything that is revered, or believed to convey spiritual power.
imagines: The final developmental stage of an insect after undergoing metamorphosis.
hydraulic: To mine using the technique of hydraulic mining.
gourd: Any of the trailing or climbing vines producing fruit with a hard rind or shell, from the genera Lagenaria and Cucurbita (in Cucurbitaceae).
leprosy: An infectious disease caused by infection by Mycobacterium leprae.
molecule: The smallest particle of a specific element or compound that retains the chemical properties of that element or compound; two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds.
nasal: A medicine that operates through the nose; an errhine.
liter: The metric unit of fluid measure, equal to one cubic decimetre. Symbols: l, L, ℓ
purchasing: To buy, obtain by payment of a price in money or its equivalent.
munro: Any Scottish mountain having a height of more than 3,000 feet; named after Sir Hugh Thomas Munro, Scottish mountaineer
